title: Runtime Context v2: compiled runtime contracts for persistent Bots
problem: orgctl render-bot built standing Bot context by concatenating every always_load file plus instructions, capabilities and boundaries, so the same invariants were repeated across many sources and standing context ran from about 9.9k to 15.4k chars per position before any task context.
desired_outcome: Persistent positions receive a compact, provider-neutral compiled runtime contract with retrieval triggers; canonical sources remain authoritative in Git; governance invariants are validated structurally; efficiency is measurable.
acceptance_criteria: Engineering Manager standing context <= 6,000 chars; product/rnd/dev-lead <= 5,000; assurance/auditor <= 5,500
Standing context is compiled, not concatenated source files
Required invariants, risk ceiling, fail-closed, memory non-authoritativeness, evidence/verification and checkpoint rules are machine-validated
Retrieval triggers exist and every previously loaded source remains reachable
Employee continuity is excluded from routine runtime context
Context size is measurable via orgctl context-report
orgctl validate, render-all and make audit pass
No approval, verification, evidence, authority or risk-ceiling requirement is weakened
nonfunctional_requirements: no canonical policy or knowledge deletion
implementation_path: external executor (Claude Code) at Owner request
